title: Dental Savings Plans vs Dental Insurance: Which Is Better?
description: Dental savings (discount) plans and dental insurance compared: how each works, waiting periods, annual maximums, in-house membership plans and who each suits.
h1: Dental savings plans vs dental insurance
intro: If you do not get dental insurance through work, you have two main choices: buy a dental insurance plan or join a dental savings plan. Here is how they compare.

image.alt: Dentist in a white shirt holding a pen at a consultation

cardText: Dental savings (discount) plans and dental insurance compared: how each works, waiting periods, annual maximums, in-house membership plans and who each suits.

sections.html:
Dental insuranceDental savings plan
Is it insurance?YesNo: a discount membership
Annual maximumUsually yesUsually none

Pre-existing conditionsMay be excludedUsually accepted
NetworkPPO or DHMO networkParticipating dentists only

Many dental practices now offer their own membership plans: a yearly or monthly fee that covers preventive visits plus a discount on other treatment. They can be good value if you are uninsured and like your dentist, but only work at that practice.

• Insurance may suit people who mainly want preventive care and can plan major work around waiting periods.
  • Savings plans may suit people who need treatment soon, have reached their annual maximum, or are on Medicare without dental coverage.

Before joining a discount plan, confirm your dentist participates. Check plan terms with your state insurance department if anything is unclear.

General information, not medical, legal or insurance advice. This post reflects the position on the date shown. Check the official sources below for the latest rules.

faqs.a: Many are, but they are not insurance. Check which dentists participate and read the terms, including cancellation rules.
